intro: Walk down a street in Chicago and you may pass a synagogue with Hebrew letters over the door, then a church with a cross on its roof. Both communities read some of the same ancient books. Both look back to Abraham. Yet they tell the story that follows in different ways, and each has a long history of its own.

In this unit you will study Judaism and Christianity the way a historian does. You will read their texts, watch their practices and follow them through exile, empire, reform and life in America. You will describe what adherents believe and do, in their own words, without deciding who is right.

By the end, you will be able to put key events in order, explain terms like covenant, Talmud, creed and Reformation, and compare how the two traditions answer the same questions. You will also find their stories in Chicago today.
bigQuestion: How did Judaism and Christianity grow from shared roots into two traditions with their own texts, practices and histories?

timeline.t: Babylon destroys the first Temple; many Jews go into exile
The Second Temple is finished in Jerusalem
Jesus is crucified in Jerusalem under Roman rule
Paul writes letters to early churches
Rabbi Judah the Prince collects the Mishnah
The Edict of Milan allows Christians to worship freely
The church splits into Catholic west and Orthodox east
Martin Luther writes the 95 Theses; the Reformation begins
Nazi Germany murders about six million Jews in the Holocaust
Martin Luther King Jr. writes the Letter from Birmingham Jail

teaching; the first five books of the Hebrew Bible
being forced to live away from your homeland
a Jewish teacher of the Torah and Jewish law
the Mishnah together with centuries of rabbis' discussions of it
the Jewish Sabbath, from Friday sunset to Saturday night
anointed one; Christians believe Jesus is the Messiah, or Christ
good news; one of the four books that tell Jesus' life

test.q: Which figure do Jews, Christians and Muslims all honor as an ancestor in faith?
test.why: All three Abrahamic traditions look back to Abraham.

test.q: What happened to the Temple in 70 CE?
test.why: Rome destroyed the Second Temple in 70 CE. Babylon destroyed the first in 586 BCE.

test.q: Which book collects Jewish oral teaching from c. 200 CE?
test.why: The Mishnah, collected c. 200 CE, wrote down Jewish oral teaching.
Passover remembers the Exodus from Egypt.

choices: Anointed one, from the Greek for Messiah
test.why: Christ comes from the Greek word for Messiah, meaning anointed one.

test.q: How do Jews and Christians differ about Jesus?
choices: Both see him as the Messiah
Christians believe he is the Messiah; Judaism does not hold this
Jews see him as the author of the Torah
test.why: Christians believe Jesus is the Messiah. Jewish tradition does not hold this belief.

test.q: Which writings are the oldest in the New Testament?
test.why: Paul's letters date to c. 50 to 60 CE, earlier than the Gospels.

test.q: What did the Edict of Milan do?
test.why: In 313 CE the Edict of Milan allowed Christians to worship freely.

choices: A break between the Catholic west and Orthodox east
test.why: In 1054, leaders of the eastern and western churches excommunicated each other.

test.q: What helped Luther's ideas spread so fast?
test.why: Printers copied his writings quickly, so they spread across Germany.

test.q: Which Jewish movement began in 1800s Germany and allows practice to change?
test.why: Reform Judaism began in Germany in the early 1800s.

test.q: Psalm 137 and the spiritual Go Down, Moses both come from people who were…
test.why: Psalm 137 speaks for exiles in Babylon; Go Down, Moses was sung by enslaved Africans in America.

test.q: Which text is a short statement of belief said in many churches?
test.why: The Nicene Creed, from 325 CE, is a short statement of Christian belief.

choices: Nazi Germany's murder of about six million Jews
The fall of the Second Temple
test.why: In the Holocaust, 1933 to 1945, Nazi Germany and its allies murdered about six million Jews.

choices: The Talmud was written in Chicago
Thomas Dorsey helped spread gospel music from a Chicago church
The Great Schism began in Chicago
test.why: Thomas Dorsey led a choir at Pilgrim Baptist Church and is called the father of gospel music.

write.prompt: Both traditions faced great loss: Jews lost the Temple in 70 CE, and early Christians faced persecution. Using two or three texts from this unit, explain how each tradition kept its faith alive, and compare the answers.
tips: Name each text you cite, such as Psalm 137, Pirkei Avot 1:1 or Galatians 3:28.
Attribute every belief: write Jews believe or Christians teach.
Compare the two traditions; do not judge which is right.
Use unit words such as exile, rabbi, Talmud, martyr and creed.
